directions: Start seed indoors 6–8 weeks before the last frost and transplant into deeply prepared, fertile soil in full sun. Copia is a striking modern heirloom, named for the American food and wine culture center in Napa where it was introduced, prized for its large, meaty fruit that ripens to a warm golden-yellow background overlaid with red marbling and streaks radiating from the blossom end. The flesh is sweet with balanced acidity and holds its shape well for slicing, making the fruit as good on a cheese board as in a sandwich. Provide sturdy staking or caging for the tall indeterminate vine, water evenly to reduce cracking, and pick fruit once fully colored for the best sweetness.

directions: Start seed indoors 6–8 weeks before the last frost and transplant into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun. Chocolate Stripes is a dark-fruited heirloom beefsteak tomato with dusky mahogany-brown skin overlaid with darker green-brown stripes radiating from the stem, and rich, complex, slightly smoky-sweet flesh characteristic of the best dark-colored heirloom tomatoes. Fruit runs large for slicing and sandwiches, and the deep coloring makes it a striking addition to a mixed heirloom tomato platter. Stake or cage the vigorous indeterminate vine well, water evenly to reduce cracking and blossom end rot, and harvest once fruit gives slightly to gentle pressure and the shoulders have darkened fully.

common_name: Djena Lee's Golden Girl Tomato (Sweet Low-Acid Yellow Heirloom)

planting.note: Start indoors 6–8 weeks before last frost and transplant after frost danger passes; this productive indeterminate vine benefits from staking and consistent watering through fruit set.

directions: Start seed indoors 6–8 weeks before the last frost and transplant into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun. Djena Lee's Golden Girl is an American heirloom yellow beefsteak tomato producing large, smooth, deep-golden fruit with sweet, mild, notably low-acid flesh that is easy on sensitive stomachs and a favorite for gardeners who find red tomatoes too sharp. It is a heavy, dependable producer for an heirloom, setting good yields of large fruit over a long season on a vigorous indeterminate vine. Stake or cage plants for support, water evenly to prevent cracking and blossom end rot, and pick fruit once the skin turns fully golden-yellow and gives slightly to gentle pressure.

common_name: Berkeley Tie Dye Tomato (Multicolor Striped Modern Heirloom)

planting.note: Start indoors 6–8 weeks before last frost and transplant after frost danger passes; the vigorous indeterminate vine benefits from strong staking and even watering to support its heavy clusters of colorful fruit.

directions: Start seed indoors 6–8 weeks before the last frost and transplant into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun. Berkeley Tie Dye is a modern specialty tomato bred for its vividly striped fruit, splashed with purple, green, red, and orange in a swirled, painterly pattern that makes it one of the most visually striking tomatoes a gardener can grow, with rich, complex, sweet-tart flesh to match its looks. It is a strong, productive indeterminate vine that sets clusters of medium-to-large fruit over a long season. Stake or cage plants securely for the heavy fruit load, water evenly to reduce cracking, and pick once the stripes have fully developed and fruit yields slightly to gentle pressure.
